newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA CUSTOMS THREATEN CRACKDOWN ON SAA FLIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA CUSTOMS THREATEN CRACKDOWN ON SAA FLIGHTS.

text.p: South African customs, worried about smuggling, may stop South African Airways international flights from taking on domestic passengers at Johannesburg for onward transport to Cape Town or Durban.

An airline spokesman said the South African Revenue Services (SARS) had said that from November 1 all international passengers would have to leave the aircraft at the first landing point, normally Johannesburg, and go through customs.
Alternatively, SAA flights could proceed from Johannesburg to Cape Town or Durban wihout taking on any domestic passengers, as some foreign airlines already do.
The move would cost SAA some 75 million rand a year in lost revenue, the spokesman said.
The SARS is concerned that drugs and other goods could be smuggled into the country by domestic passengers who received them from international travellers.
Discussions between SAA and the customs service are continuing.
